title: arXiv Physics — Tuesday, 3 November 2026
global_caveat: This is an inferred notable-paper ordering, not an official arXiv trending chart; arXiv publishes no trending ranking, and citation evidence for very recent papers is limited.

sections.title: The Neptunian ridge through the lens of TESS
sections.abstract: Using TESS occurrence posteriors, the author finds a roughly twofold excess of 5–8-Earth-radius planets at 3–6-day periods, consistent with the ridge previously seen by Kepler.
sections.claimed_result: The author reports that the ridge's occurrence density is about twice that of the denser neighboring region (J = 2.05 with −0.44/+0.52 uncertainty; 99.9% posterior support), while evidence for an asymmetric ridge profile remains weak.
sections.evidence_type: Observational; TESS occurrence posteriors for FGK main-sequence stars, based on Sectors 1–55 and compared with earlier Kepler occurrence estimates.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A distinct survey's TESS occurrence data recover a concrete population feature, with a quantified 3.1σ-equivalent posterior contrast and explicit comparison against six occurrence profiles.
sections.unique_caveat: The inferred ridge shape depends on occurrence-rate posteriors and profile choices; the author says the asymmetry is weakly supported and calls for more precise occurrence measurements.

sections.title: Ultrafast X-ray-induced dephasing of valence electrons
sections.abstract: In silicon, energy-chirped X-ray diffraction measurements show that valence-bond coherence is lost in under 20 femtoseconds, before substantial lattice motion and even at low ionization fluence.
sections.claimed_result: The authors attribute the rapid loss of valence-sensitive scattering to valence-bond dephasing and argue that probing pristine valence-electron structure requires pulses shorter than the roughly 50-fs standard discussed in the paper.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; broadband, energy-chirped X-ray pulses probe elemental silicon at the SwissFEL Bernina instrument, comparing a structurally forbidden reflection with a simultaneously measured Bragg peak.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A direct time-resolved experiment separates valence-sensitive forbidden reflections from core-dominated Bragg peaks and reports a sub-20-fs effect with implications for ultrafast crystallography.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors describe their fluence model as phenomenological and say quantitative treatment of the forbidden-reflection suppression requires explicit nonequilibrium excited-state calculations.

sections.title: Mercury (Hg): a relativistic N-body simulation for Horndeski gravity
sections.abstract: The authors introduce a relativistic particle-mesh N-body code that evolves matter, metric fields, and an additional scalar degree of freedom across the general linear Horndeski alpha-basis.
sections.claimed_result: The authors show that, in the luminal Horndeski models considered, a running effective Planck mass changes gravitational slip and vector/tensor friction terms, with corresponding changes in the effective dark-energy density-contrast power spectrum.
sections.evidence_type: Computational; relativistic particle-mesh simulations for six representative Horndeski models, checked against hi_class linear predictions and earlier k-essence/KGB limits.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The work spans cosmology, gravitation, and computational physics through three category listings and provides a reusable simulation framework, with validation against hi_class in the linear regime and recovery of established limits.
sections.unique_caveat: This is an intermediate framework: the paper retains linear Horndeski scalar-field dynamics, so nonlinear scalar self-interactions and screening are not yet incorporated.

sections.title: Fermi surface and field-induced Lifshitz transition in the antiferromagnet NbMnP exhibiting an anomalous Hall effect
sections.abstract: Shubnikov–de Haas measurements on NbMnP match calculated low-field Fermi-surface orbits and show a changing oscillation spectrum at high fields that the authors interpret as a Lifshitz transition.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report that the low-field oscillation frequencies agree with the calculated bands, while the spectrum evolves at high field in a manner indicating a field-induced change in Fermi-surface topology; measured effective masses are about twice the band masses.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; Shubnikov–de Haas oscillations in NbMnP single crystals, measured to 17.5 T and 41.5 T and compared with first-principles band calculations.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: High-field measurements extend to 41.5 T and combine quantum-oscillation data with first-principles calculations grounded in a neutron-diffraction magnetic structure.
sections.unique_caveat: The microscopic reconstruction is not fully resolved; the authors note that NbMnP's noncollinear magnetism prevents a simple majority/minority-spin interpretation of the field evolution.

sections.title: Imaging the Current Distribution in Superconducting Transition-Edge Sensors with Scanning SQUID Microscopy
sections.abstract: Scanning SQUID microscopy maps superconducting regions and bias-dependent current redistribution in two molybdenum-gold X-ray transition-edge sensor designs.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report bias-dependent reconfiguration of current paths that tracks changes in the superconducting regions of the sensors.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; scanning superconducting quantum interference device microscopy measures local diamagnetic response and Oersted fields in two MoAu X-ray TES designs under voltage bias.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct spatial imaging links superconducting-state changes to transport-current rearrangements, and the three category listings connect condensed-matter device physics with detector instrumentation; the authors also note submission to Applied Physics Letters.
sections.unique_caveat: The measurements cover two device designs; how broadly the observed mesoscale current patterns generalize across TES geometries remains to be tested.

sections.title: Active-subspace learning reveals dominant parameter directions in nuclear observables
sections.abstract: Active-subspace analysis finds that a single direction in a 17-parameter interaction space captures over 99% of gradient-based variation for selected oxygen-isotope observables and substantially improves a calcium emulator.
sections.claimed_result: The authors use many-body calculations to identify dominant low-energy-constant directions for oxygen energies and radii and show that these directions can improve Gaussian-process emulation for 48Ca.
sections.evidence_type: Computational; ab initio calculations for oxygen isotopes and Hartree–Fock calculations for 48Ca, with active-subspace sensitivity analysis and Gaussian-process emulation.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper reports over 99% concentration in one parameter direction for each tested observable and more than a 100-fold emulator-error improvement in its Hartree–Fock demonstration.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported parameter compression is demonstrated on selected observables and interactions; transfer to other nuclei, observables, and interaction choices is not established here.

sections.title: Quantum channel tomography: optimal bounds in the near-boundary regime
sections.abstract: The authors close the near-boundary query-complexity gap for quantum-channel tomography and distinguish abrupt from gradual Heisenberg-to-classical scaling under two error norms.
sections.claimed_result: For bounded Kraus rank, the authors derive optimal query-complexity bounds near dilation rate one, finding a sudden loss of Heisenberg scaling for diamond norm error but a gradual transition for Choi trace norm error.
sections.evidence_type: Theoretical; query-complexity lower and upper bounds for black-box quantum-channel tomography.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper addresses an explicitly unresolved regime and claims optimal lower and upper bounds, with cross-listing in quantum information and information theory.
sections.unique_caveat: The result is mathematical and asymptotic under the paper's stated channel-rank and error-norm assumptions; it is not an experimental tomography demonstration.

sections.title: Tracing source imprints on the gravitational direct wave
sections.abstract: A generalized steepest-descent calculation relates the direct component of black-hole ringdown to the plunging source trajectory and reproduces numerical waveforms across the plunge.
sections.claimed_result: The authors show that the full frequency-dependent black-hole response localizes the source kernel better than a standard rational filter and that complex continuation of Teukolsky source variables yields a semianalytic direct wave matching numerical integration.
sections.evidence_type: Theoretical; black-hole perturbation theory using Teukolsky source variables, waveform filtering, and numerical integration as the comparison.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper introduces a refined waveform-filtering kernel and a semianalytic treatment that the authors compare with numerical integration throughout the plunge; its comment says it is to be submitted to Physical Review D Letters.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a waveform-theory result rather than an observation; the authors say the connection between source trajectory and observed direct wave remains incompletely understood.

sections.title: Full edge control of bulk energy gap in armchair graphene nanoribbons
sections.abstract: The authors show theoretically that edge-only hopping changes can fully tune the bulk gap in a family of armchair graphene nanoribbons, including with Hubbard interactions.
sections.claimed_result: The authors derive full boundary control of the energy gap for the Nw = 3p + 2 ribbon family, persisting with Hubbard interactions and independent of ribbon width within that family.
sections.evidence_type: Theoretical; analysis of armchair graphene nanoribbon hopping models, including Hubbard interactions.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The work bridges condensed-matter and lattice-field-theory categories and offers a specific mechanism—cancellation of bulk hopping contributions—for its strong boundary-control claim.
sections.unique_caveat: The result is model-based and the abstract gives no experimental demonstration of the proposed gap control in fabricated ribbons.
